provider_if_inherited: Transaction platform vendor; email provider; accounting SaaS vendor
implementation_statement: The vendors provide account management functions. The owner creates and removes the coordinator's transaction platform account and the bookkeeper's accountant login. Gaps: the coordinator also uses the owner's own mailbox credentials; the coordinator's platform account can open every file; no periodic account review.
evidence: Platform user list; accounting user list; P07 IA-2 test

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the broker-owner is the only escrow signatory and the only online banking user, so duties cannot be separated. The outside bookkeeper, who has no online banking access, prepares the monthly escrow reconciliation from bank statements, and the owner reviews, signs, and dates it (r. 61J2-14.012(2)). Before any outgoing escrow payment the owner confirms the instruction by callback and records it on the escrow ledger (POL-01 8.4). Title companies and closing attorneys hold most deposits. Gap: the coordinator acts under the owner's mailbox identity until a separate login is in use (POAM-001).
evidence: Signed monthly escrow reconciliations; escrow ledger callback entries; POL-01 8.4; POAM-001
regulatory_driver: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61J2-14.012(2); Fla. Stat. 475.25(1)(d)1.

implementation_statement: The laptop locks after 5 minutes idle and the phone after 30 seconds; both need the passcode or password to unlock.

The phone has a passcode and is encrypted by it. Gaps: photos of driver licenses and pre-approval letters arrive by text and stay in the message history and camera roll; remote wipe is not turned on; the lockbox app on the same phone opens listed homes.

Neither the owner nor the coordinator has had security training. Both will complete a short course with a business email compromise module, and the owner will subscribe to monthly reminders, by 2026-11-30.
Training will cover spotting altered wire instructions, look-alike domains, and fake sign-in pages, and how to report them (POL-01 9.6). The May 2026 near miss is the first case study.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Nobody has reviewed the email sign-in history, mailbox rules, or the platform access log. Starting 2026-10, the owner reviews them every Monday (10 minutes) and logs the review; the provider's alerts for new forwarding rules and unusual sign-ins go to the owner's phone.

Compensating control (one-person business): the broker-owner is the only administrator, so the audit records relied on are the email sign-in history and the platform access log that the providers keep, not files the owner keeps. Gap: the security log and the escrow ledger are only in SYS-02 with no independent backup until 2026-11-30 (POAM-007).
evidence: Email sign-in history; platform access log; POAM-007

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the broker-owner designed, operates, and assessed the controls, and P07 states that independence is limited. The IT technician ran the 2026 tests under a confidentiality agreement but also supports the laptop and router. POL-01 4.5 requires the IT technician to check the settings independently at least every second year, by 2027-08-31 (P03 G-034). The platform vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report (P09) covers inherited controls. Base CA-2 is the August self-assessment.
evidence: P07 assessment-plan.md (independence statement); POL-01 4.5; P03 G-034; P09

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): there is no change board, so under CM-3(g) the change control element is the security log. Every change to account security, sharing, forwarding, or network settings is noted with the date and reason (POL-01 7.8). Gap: setting changes were made ad hoc and not recorded; the log starts by 2026-09-30 (P03 G-032).

The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gaps: no backup broker arrangement, no sealed recovery codes, and no answer from the bank about an incapacitated signatory (due 2026-12-31).

The vendors back up their platforms (inherited; the platform's SOC 2 system description states a 1-hour RPO). Owner responsibility: no independent backup of the mailbox, files, or the escrow ledger spreadsheet, so deleted items can be recovered only within the provider's retention window.
evidence: Platform SOC 2 report; email retention settings
regulatory_driver: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61J2-14.012(1); N53-R01 benchmark (314.4(c)(2))

implementation_statement: The owner, coordinator, and bookkeeper have their own platform and accounting accounts. Gap: the coordinator signs in to the owner's mailbox as the owner, so actions in the mailbox cannot be told apart.
evidence: Platform and accounting user lists; P07 test

implementation_statement: Email (the owner is also the domain administrator) and online banking require a text-message code. Gaps: the broker administrator account on the transaction platform has no MFA; text codes can be relayed by a fake sign-in page and are forwarded to the coordinator. Move to an authenticator app or security key by 2026-09-30.

provider_if_inherited: Transaction platform vendor; e-signature vendor; accounting SaaS vendor
implementation_statement: The coordinator's platform account, the owner's e-signature account, and the accounting logins use a password only. All offer MFA; the owner turns it on and requires it for the coordinator and bookkeeper by 2026-09-30.

Passwords are saved in the browser and two are reused across accounts; the email password is known to the coordinator. A password manager with unique passphrases replaces them by 2026-09-30, and the email password is changed once the coordinator has a separate login.

The business email compromise runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-09-15. Gaps: the bank fraud desk number and the insurer claims contact are not yet confirmed, and the runbook has not been walked through (due 2026-10-31).

Paper with client information is cross-cut shredded at home. Gaps: the previous phone was traded in during 2025 without a documented wipe, and there is no written method for wiping or destroying devices.
evidence: Self-attestation; shredder in the home office

implementation_statement: POL-01 section 9 sets rules for the owner and, through the engagement terms, for the coordinator. Gap: a family member still used the laptop under the owner's login during fieldwork; a separate family account is due 2026-09-30.
First risk assessment completed 2026-08-21 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed each August and after a major change.

The SaaS vendors' terms include security and breach notice commitments, and the platform vendor's SOC 2 report was reviewed on 2026-08-19. Gaps: no written security or breach notice terms with the coordinator or bookkeeper; the screening service and the AI writing assistant were never reviewed.

The laptop host firewall is on. Gaps: the ISP router keeps its default admin password, and work, family, and smart-home devices share one network. A separate work network and a changed admin password are due 2026-10-31.

All SaaS and banking sessions use TLS (inherited). Gaps: escrow wire instructions, driver license images, and bank statements travel as ordinary email attachments and texts. They move to the platform's secure document sharing by 2026-10-31.

The laptop has full-disk encryption and the phone is encrypted by its passcode. The SaaS vendors encrypt stored data (platform SOC 2 report). Owner responsibility: keep encryption on and the recovery key offline.
evidence: Device encryption status; platform SOC 2 report

implementation_statement: The SaaS vendors patch their applications and automatic updates are on for the laptop and phone. Gap: the router firmware has not been updated since 2023.
The built-in antivirus runs real-time scanning with automatic updates on the laptop. Owner responsibility: keep it on and act on alerts.

The email provider filters spam and phishing on inbound and outbound mail and quarantines detections, with automatic updates. It does not stop look-alike domains or a taken-over mailbox; those are handled by AU-6 and the wire verification rule (POL-01 8.4).

Client files are kept indefinitely, with extra copies in email, downloads, and the phone. POL-01 8.7 sets a retention schedule: one complete file per transaction kept for the 5 years Fla. Stat. 475.5015 requires, then destroyed; extra copies of identity documents and screening reports deleted within 30 days after closing or the rental decision; first purge by 2026-12-31.
